fracture.basis: One apartment, forward order marked by 'the next day', 'approximately six months later', 'later that night'

dread.basis: A tsunami, a falling moon and the threat of turning to sea foam, all named and then defused by Gran Mamare's test

cruelty.basis: The one antagonist is a father searching frantically for his daughter, and he ends by respecting her choice

irony.basis: The bubble, the kiss and the restored balance of nature are meant exactly as shown

ambiguity.basis: The test is passed, the transformation completed, the ships return to port

fracture.basis: Continuous forward story from the jellyfish escape to the kiss

dread.basis: Monastery encircled, escape means slaughter, liquid spreading, recurring shared warning-dream — threat is continuous from arrival

cruelty.basis: Possessed infect and kill team, anyone leaving is slaughtered, but harm is impersonal contagion, not dwelt-on suffering

irony.basis: Anti-God, tachyon dreams and Christ-as-extraterrestrial are advanced straight; the wise-cracking student is the only distance

ambiguity.basis: Threat is fully explained and sealed, but the closing dream-within-dream and Brian's hand at the mirror settle nothing

fracture.basis: One forward order; only the transmitted future-dream and the opening historical prologue displace anything

dread.basis: Collapse is political and already known; the pistol-for-suicide line marks doom, not expected bodily harm

cruelty.basis: Profanity and blame among staff, but the film supplies childhood, dead brothers and illness as mitigation

ambiguity.basis: Responsibility for the assassination is only 'hinted' and 'implied'; who Kissinger is is never adjudicated

fracture.basis: Framed in Dec 1973 with tapes triggering flashbacks to 1972, childhood and the vice presidency; real funeral footage after the end

dread.basis: Recent car crash, Linda's worry over his state of mind, and Ben's encouragement point steadily at the death named in the title

cruelty.basis: Firing, the forgotten job interview and the Boston betrayal wound, but harm is largely self-inflicted and the film stays close to Willy

irony.basis: Biff's 'we are a dime a dozen' speech and the hug are played straight; no gap between image and meaning

ambiguity.basis: Boston is revealed, the suicide's motive stated, and the funeral fixes where Biff and Happy each land

fracture.basis: Same events retold three times with different actors, motives and outcomes; the telling is permutation, not sequence

dread.basis: Cannon, machine guns and mounted pursuers, yet every setback (Samurai off the train, dropped equipment) is improvised past

cruelty.basis: Dutchman's wife executed and rebels die covering the escape, but killing is dispatched quickly and not lingered on

irony.basis: The revolution's cause is taken at face value; the closing laughter is acquiescence, not undercutting

ambiguity.basis: Gold delivered, Dutchman's motive explained aloud, every man's allegiance settled before the credits

fracture.basis: Hire, assemble, rescue, escape, rob, split — one order, one direction, no displacement

irony.basis: Bioscope, candy man and the distant train whistle are offered as simple joys with no distance from them

fracture.basis: Straight chronological passage through seasons, two deaths and departure; no displacement of any kind

fracture.basis: A journey frame broken into discrete ceremonies across decades, entered by flashback and closing on a further flashback

irony.basis: The shrine, the nursery rhyme and the hypnosis reveal are played for straight gothic effect

ambiguity.basis: Killer named, motive (Kathleen's drowning) explained, and Billy shot dead on the spot

fracture.basis: Boat, castle, murders, investigation, capture — one forward line; Kathleen's death is exposition, not a displaced scene

irony.basis: The priest's hypocrisy is exposed as content, not as distance — the acolyte's disillusion is presented in earnest

ambiguity.basis: He refuses to speak under interrogation and the summary can only say he 'felt misunderstood'; the leap from the train ends it unanswered

fracture.basis: Interrogation frame with stacked flashbacks — the temple arrival, and memories nested inside those (mocking, the mother's adultery, the funeral)

dread.basis: Police tailing, a murder charge and a creditor gangster run under the trip, but the sting fails and the mood stays domestic

ambiguity.basis: A body found and Sang-hyeon 'cannot be found', then a laundry van with her photo drives off — identity and fate withheld

fracture.basis: Continuous forward telling with one clean three-year jump to the coda

dread.basis: Two terminal cancers, a suicide attempt in a parking lot and a gun to the head — but crises erupt rather than loom.

cruelty.basis: Adults block a child from the bathroom until he wets himself; Rick berates him — yet the film ends forgiving nearly everyone.

irony.basis: Frogs fall from the sky and Claudia glances into the camera and smiles — a designed rupture over otherwise unguarded feeling.

fracture.basis: Interlocking strands cross-cut but run one forward day; the frogs land simultaneously across all of them.

dread.basis: From the derelict apartment onward every visit expects a corpse or the creature; ends with sirens, planes and explosions.

irony.basis: The film reel of the ballet student is presented as evidence, not commentary; the doppelgänger is played wholly straight.

ambiguity.basis: The creature, the miscarried 'Faith', Helen's green eyes and the final doppelgänger are never explained or reconciled.

fracture.basis: Strict forward chronology; the only inset is Heinrich's film reel, watched in sequence.

ambiguity.basis: Whether the fires are signal fires or burning corn husks is never settled, and he walks into them and is shot.

fracture.basis: One man's continuous march, closed by a title reading February 1945.

irony.basis: A play about masochism rehearsed by two people who become it, bracketed twice by the same Book of Judith epigraph.

ambiguity.basis: Vanda's script, costumes, lightboard command and 'guess' about the fiancée are never explained; she invokes Dionysus and leaves.

fracture.basis: One evening, one theatre, forward order; the only layering is script-reading inside the scene.

irony.basis: Martial philosophy is delivered without a wink; the voice-over mourns Gong Er's opium and lost Baguazhang straight.

ambiguity.basis: Voice-over supplies the missing facts — the injury, the opium, the secrets lost — and dates every death.

fracture.basis: Opens mid-rainstorm fight then flashes back to age seven; the 1940 train-station duel is withheld until after the 1950 meeting.

cruelty.basis: Opens on gang rape and the murder of her family and the slaughter of the priestesses, then converts it all into quest motivation.

irony.basis: The vow, the Talisman and the sword-fight-as-courtship are all meant literally; the film stands behind its mythology.

ambiguity.basis: Villain run through into lava, Talisman destroyed, castle collapses, couple kisses, prince rides home to rebuild.

fracture.basis: One quest in one direction; even the origin is told first, in order.

fracture.basis: Framed by the 1939 funeral, then 1938 China repeatedly interrupted by 1925, 1927, early 1930s and Spain.

ambiguity.basis: The Blue Letter is read aloud and explains the whole scheme; Mussburger is institutionalised and the couple reconciles.

fracture.basis: December 1958 forward to 1959; the only reach back is a letter written before the film starts.

irony.basis: Earnest to the last frame — the world stops, war halts, and she says 'Listen'

fracture.basis: Two strands run in parallel until they converge, plus a recovered childhood-abduction memory

irony.basis: He reads her unmailed letter aloud almost perfectly and she accepts the proposal, played entirely straight

fracture.basis: Single forward order with one signposted jump, 'thirteen months later'
